subject: programming-and-data-structures

chosen.title: Programming in C - subject chapter (GATE Overflow for GATE CSE, Volume 2)
covers: sizeof as an operator over types, and the struct and union size bounds
integer promotion and the usual arithmetic conversions
storage-class binding, scope and lifetime
pointers, the double pointer, and the wild and dangling pointer pitfalls
structures, unions, member access and padding
dynamic memory signatures
programming constructs and their pitfalls
chosen.why: the only GATE-oriented chapter found that walks the whole topic in one voice with an explicit pitfall list per concept; it carries the enumeration and the trap fields of nine of the thirteen cards

chosen.title: C Programming Fundamentals: Complete Guide with Worked Examples for GATE and Placements
covers: the GATE size convention and the format specifiers
signed-char wrap and integer division
precedence, and the unsequenced-modification warning
do-while, switch fall-through and a continue trace
pointer arithmetic and call by value
chosen.why: the only source read this run that gives worked outputs for the conversion traps and states plainly that i++ + ++i has no trustworthy answer, which is the basis of the sequence-point card

chosen.title: Pointers in C for GATE: Memory Diagrams and Output Traces
covers: the box-and-arrow pointer model and the double-pointer trace
the array walk and the sizeof contrast
the failing swap and the working pointer swap
*p++ against (*p)++
dangling pointers and the read-only string literal
chosen.why: read end to end, and the only source that works the *p++ precedence rule and the sizeof-of-a-pointer-versus-array contrast through concrete traces

chosen.title: Pointers, arrays and strings in C - GATE notes and 11 solved PYQs
covers: the GATE size and layout conventions
the three no-decay exceptions and the sizeof rules
the address formula and the pointer-difference rule
the two-dimensional parameter adjustment
the malloc, calloc and realloc contracts
chosen.why: the only source that states the three exceptions to array decay as a numbered list and gives the failure behaviour of realloc, both of which the cards needed and the other sources did not state precisely

chosen.title: Functions, parameter passing, scope and storage classes - GATE notes and 7 solved PYQs
covers: call by value and the order of events in a call
the array-parameter exception and the unsequenced-argument warning
block and file scope, shadowing, static against dynamic scoping
the four storage classes with duration, default value and linkage
the constant-initialiser rule and the register address rule
chosen.why: the only source read this run with a complete storage-class table and an explicit statement that scope and lifetime are separate properties, which three cards depend on

chosen.title: C mein Programming - chapter notes (Devanagari)
covers: the preprocessor as pure textual substitution and the SQ(x) parentheses trap
the NUL-terminated char array as the definition of a C string
arr[i] defined as *(arr + i) and the array-parameter sizeof trap
struct padding and the union size
the three heap bugs and argc and argv
chosen.why: the only readable non-English source, and the only one read this run that states the macro-parenthesis trap and the include guard at all; its four translated sentences are marked as translated on the cards that use them

chosen.title: Problem Solving through Programming in C - 12-week course layout (IIT Kharagpur)
covers: the teaching order: variables and data types, expressions and operators, branching, loops, arrays, strings, functions and parameter passing by value, structures and pointers
chosen.why: read only for its week list, to check that the subtopic enumeration below is complete; no sentence of any card rests on it

the lecture pages publish an English AI summary and chapters with timestamps, but the lessons themselves are behind an enrolment wall; with six readable texts in hand there was no need to lean on a summary of a lecture that could not be heard, and no card quotes one

left unread this run because the six chosen sources already covered every subtopic with GATE framing, and the same hosts have answered 502 to this sandbox in earlier runs; no claim rests on them
the Hindi C course that matched the topic lesson for lesson (storage classes, pointers and structures, unions) is behind a subscription, so no text was readable

readable Hindi pages on dynamic memory, but generic programming tutorials with no GATE framing, no PYQ and no pointer or structure treatment; the CareerCraft Labs chapter covers the same ground and more, so these were not used

paywalled, a 1700-question MCQ bank rather than teaching, a generic notebook, and a beginner pointer tutorial respectively; none of them states a GATE-relevant rule the chosen sources do not state better

used to locate questions and to corroborate answers, never as the source of a card; their numbering disagrees with each other and with the printed papers (the 2000 struct question is Q.34 on SolutionsAdda and Q.36 on ExamSIDE, the 2008 double-pointer question is Q.60 on GATE Overflow and Q.25 on ExamSIDE's topic page), and every such disagreement is recorded in the PYQ record rather than resolved

standard_refs: Kernighan and Ritchie, The C Programming Language, 2nd edition, chapters 1 to 6 - cited as the standard treatment, not fetched this run
ISO/IEC 9899 (C99, and C11 for _Thread_local) for the sequencing, promotion, storage-duration and undefined-behaviour rules - cited, not fetched
GATE Overflow question pages for the thirteen recorded PYQs, each carrying an accepted answer
language_note: One of the seven chosen sources is Hindi (Devanagari), read in part and translated. Every card, caption, check and label published here is English, and each card that uses a sentence from that chapter names the translation in its source line. No card is a translation of a lecture, because no lecture transcript was readable this run.
